examples.text:
How to read this canvas: one row per journey. Each row starts with a map: the arrows show which button leads where, and where it branches. Then the screens, numbered left to right, and a note at the end.

All names and figures are made-up examples, not real data.

flow1.text: Flow 1 · Closing the day  (manager or supervisor)

flow1-note.text:
Today → End of day → fill in each section → ready to send? → day closed.

Only a section not done stops sending; anything unusual is a tap on It's right. The send button names the day and the figure.

Phone first; the desktop board is the same day on a laptop.

flow2-note.text:
Checks: what needs fixing first, then the day's lists.

Switch site and Search work from every screen.

flow3-note.text:
Stock → (full count: pick the next area) → count one item at a time → ready to send? → 'Order what's low' straight away → head office sees it.

Anyone can count. Corrections after sending need supervisor or above. Staff never see money.

flow4.text: Flow 4 · Head office checks the night  (desktop)

flow4-note.text:
Head office opens All sites after close: what needs a look, then each site.

C · Finance table is the one built in the app. A and B were the other options; the first board is the earlier version.

flow5.text: Flow 5 · Health and safety  (anyone → head office)

flow5-note.text:
Due checks on the main card → fire alarm test one question at a time → anyone reports an accident → head office sees every site.

A failed check raises a repair. An injury that keeps someone off work more than 7 days must be reported to the HSE within 15 days (RIDDOR).

flow6-note.text:
What's due → one piece of equipment and its history → log the visit with the certificate → head office sees every certificate.

Reminders 30 and 7 days before. 'Keeps breaking' = 3 or more call-outs in 6 months.

flow7.text: Flow 7 · Ordering and waste  (site → head office)

flow7-note.text:
Order: already filled in from par levels, so it's one tap to send.
Delivery: everything starts ticked; tap only what didn't come (shorts become credits to chase).
Waste: pick the item; amount and reason are filled in from what's usual.
Head office: the answer in a sentence, then Accept.

Accepting a price updates stock values and dish costs.

flow8.text: Flow 8 · Recipes and dish costing  (kitchen → head office)

flow8-note.text:
Kitchen sees the recipe with no prices, one step at a time. Each stock item shows which dishes use it and how long it will last, with Order more. Head office sees cost and GP per dish and the fix as one button.

The allergen record stays the source of truth: a mismatch is flagged, never changed for you.

flow9-note.text: Each site's colour shows on its badge, main card and progress circles. Green, amber and red stay for status.

principles.text:
How the screens are kept simple

• One job per screen, one obvious button (Hick's law: fewer choices, faster decisions).
• Filled in for you: orders, deliveries and waste start with the likely answer, so most tasks are one or two taps (defaults).
• Only the exceptions: lists show what needs action; the rest folds into one line (progressive disclosure).
• The answer first: head office cards say what's going on in a sentence, then the detail.
• Show, don't make people read: bars instead of numbers to compare (recognition over recall).
• Big targets near the thumb, status always in words, and nothing locks you in: Back is always there.

flow11-note.text:
Start from who is asking (inspector, accountant or HMRC, HSE or insurer, staff and pay, a whole site), not from a list of record types. The app picks the records, the format and the dates.

Keep periods researched 13 Nov 2026: accounts and VAT 6 years; tips 3 years; holiday pay 6 years (from Apr 2026); minimum wage 6 years; right to work: employment + 2 years; accident book 3 years; waste transfer notes 2 years. Details and sources: docs/reports/next-modules-scope.md §6.

flow12.text: Flow 10 · Home as widgets  (staff, supervisors, managers)

flow12-note.text:
Main card first (managers: tonight's net and Up next; staff: their checks). Then widgets: Checklists, End of day, Stock, Recipes, Food safety. Everything at the bottom lists the rest.

Each person can hide, add and reorder widgets; Reset goes back to their role's default. Sizes are fixed so it always looks tidy.

Spec: docs/specs/bento-home/SPEC.md

flow13.text: Flow 10b · Other ways to lay out the home widgets  (manager, Bunso)

flow13-note.text:
Five other layouts for the same widgets, all at 18:40 on a Thursday with the same example figures.

A · Bento: numbers first, tiles of mixed sizes.
B · Timeline: widgets sit at the time they're due, with a Now line.
C · Rings: three rings to close (checklists, end of day report, food safety), then what closes them.
D · By shift: Opening, Service and Closing each get their own widgets; switches by itself.
E · Smart stack: one swipeable widget, most urgent on top, plus quick actions and recent activity.

All can still be customised (board 3): drag to reorder, tap – to hide.
